sources.title: Recursive and iterative sorted-list merge deterministic Java fixture

claims.text: The repository source explicitly requires merging two ascending linked lists, providing both recursive and iterative implementations, and comparing their stack-space cost. Node type, language, input mutability, and equal-key stability are not preserved source requirements.

Under the explicitly labeled Java reference contract that reuses input data nodes, both recursive and iterative implementations produce the sorted multiset union for all bounded generated sorted-list pairs plus integer extremes; null inputs, duplicates, identity reuse, and absence of cycles are checked deterministically.

Each implementation consumes at most one input node per decision, so both are O(m+n) time; the recursive control state can accumulate to linear call depth while the iterative implementation keeps only a constant number of references. This complexity statement is derived from the shown implementation, not from an unstated source constraint.
